content.comment_body: Hello [company_name] Support Team, I am working on integrating a [company_name] [product_name] (version [version_no]) with an MQTT cloud service. The PLC correctly receives values or commands sent from MQTTX when I declare a variable named "edge_command_k" that accepts 0 or 1 as inputs, provided the JSON format includes { "payload": [ { "state": { "edge_command_k": { "value": [1] } } } ], "command_name": "TurnOnLight", "correlation_id": "abc123" }. In this structure, the inclusion of the "state" key appears necessary for the PLC to recognize and process the command. However, if I send the message in the format { "payload": [ { "edge_command_k": { "value": [1] } } ], "command_name": "TurnOnLight", "correlation_id": "abc123" }—which omits the "state" keyword—the PLC does not parse or accept the value. Is there a way to configure the PLC to read inputs without requiring the "state" keyword, or are there alternative solutions? Thank you.

analysis.insight_summary: The user encountered a limitation when connecting a [product_name] PLC to an MQTT cloud service. The PLC only processes variable values in JSON payloads if the structure includes a 'state' key; omitting it causes the message to be ignored. This impacts how flexibly messages can be crafted for cloud integration.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the [product_name] PLC to parse and accept input values from MQTT messages regardless of whether the JSON payload includes the 'state' keyword, aiming for more flexibility in their integration.
